links.reason: Kuruntokai 320 says நக்கதோர் பழியு மிலமே of a different heroine, and its drying fish and prawns (மீன் உணங்கல், இறவின் வாடல்) are only the epithet of the துறைவன், not a place where she sat; Kainnilai 54's இறவுணங்கல் is where she guarded the catch. Two speakers in two situations are not incompatible claims, and the drying ground is not 'the scene of an innocence' in 320.

Ainkurunuru 9 wishes கேண்மை அம்பல் ஆகற்க and Kural 1143 welcomes ஊரறிந்த கெளவை as பெறாஅது பெற்றன்ன; the contrast of the women's dread and the man's relish is real. But it is two speakers with different stakes rather than two incompatible claims, so the tension type is loose.

Natrinai 335 lists the sea (பொங்கு திரைப் புணரியும் பாடு ஓவாதே, ஓதமும் பெயரும்) among what makes the night unbearable; Ainthinai Ezhupathu 60 makes it a fellow sufferer (எம்போல் ... முந்நீர் துஞ்சாதது) given her own cause. The shift from cause to companion is specific and true to both.

Natrinai 252 lines 3-4 (இறந்து செயின அல்லது அரும் பொருட் கூட்டம் இருந்தோர்க்கு இல்) restate Kural 616 closely, and வினை இடை விலங்கல போலும் shows the plan checked by her beauty. But that delay does not limit the Kural's claim that effort yields wealth; the poem applies the maxim, so 'marks the limit of the rule' overstates.

தெரிவிலர் தீங்குழல் ஊதும் பொழுது does make the herders unaware of the pain their pipe causes, which adds something to Kural 1228's கொல்லும் படை. But the verse is a fragment whose last word breaks at அரித, so the sense the teaches builds on cannot be confirmed.
links.text_issue: Kainnilai 35 lines 1-2 are lost and line 4 breaks off at அரித.

links.reason: Both Idaikkadanar homecoming speeches to the charioteer are real kin, and விருந்தெதிர் கொள (Akam 374) and விருந்து விருப்புறூஉம் (Natrinai 221) both use விருந்து. But in 221 விருந்து is an epithet of the wife, not a placing of the hero as master; the poem's goal is the son's வந்தீக எந்தை. The guest/master contrast is built on a thin word difference.

The cock as enemy of the lovers' night is shared (Akam 122 மனைச்செறி கோழி; Kuruntokai 107 சேவல்) and both mention இல் எலி. But in Akam 122 the rat-eater is the owl (இல்எலி வல்சி ... கூகை), in 107 the wildcat (இல்லெலி பார்க்கும் பிள்ளை வெருகு), so the curse does not send the cock to 'the very rat-hunters of the courtship poem'.

Both Paranar poems use Nannan for the friend's purpose, one as model of hard scheming (நறுமா கொன்று ... கோசர்), one as type of cruelty (பெண்கொலை புரிந்த நன்னன்). But 292 says only புனல்தரு பசுங்காய், not that the fruit was of the mango, so 'two halves of one tale' rests on tradition outside the poems.

Ainkurunuru 113 does pair the town's word (ஊரார் பெண்டென மொழிய) with the mother (அன்னாய் என்றனள் அன்னை), as Kural 1147 pairs ஊரவர் கெளவை with அன்னைசொல். But the girl's வெம்மை is an evasion, not the Kural's metaphor of manure and water, and the claim that the couplet's metaphor 'began as' this cover story is unsupported.

The slipping bangle and wasting shoulders (ஒண்டொடி நெகிழச் சாஅய் மென் தோள் பசப்பது; பைந்தொடி சோரும் ... தோள்) are a stock sign shared across akam. The observation that Ainkurunuru 28 uses the sign as evidence against the goddess (உண்துறை அணங்கு) is true, but the pairing rests largely on the shared symptom.
links.text_issue: Ainkurunuru 28 line 1's conditional is compressed; the marker flagged the sense.

links.reason: Kuruntokai 141 asks him not to come (ஆரிரு ணடுநாள் ... வாரலோ) because the tiger waits; Kuruntokai 153 has her heart, once frightened of a hill owl or monkey, go to him through ஆரிருட் கங்குல் along the slope. The pairing shows the night-danger plea is fear for him, not a prudence she herself keeps; true and specific.

Both heroines address the crab (கொடுந்தாள் அலவ; அலவ), one asking it not to trample the chariot's tracks, one to carry word; the shared addressee is meaningful. But neither poem says the crab 'alone moves where the lover moved'; Akam 170 gives as reason only that grove, backwater and punnai will not speak.

Kural 1081 wavers whether she is அணங்கு, peahen or woman; Ainkurunuru 191 knows her as a shore girl by her conch bangles and backwater flowers and says she is வரையர மகளிரின் அரியள். One uses the divine comparison for bewilderment, the other for distance of attainment; a specific contrast.

Ainkurunuru 461's friend says நின்துறந்து அமைகுவர் அல்லர் வெற்றி வேந்தன் பாசறையோரே; Akam 364's heroine, with the same கார்தொடங்கின்றே and the king's பாசறை, says நம்மும் உள்ளார். The two claims about the absent man contradict, and the teaches correctly locates the difference in the speaker.

Both poems join bees and the fragrance of her hair (Kuruntokai 2 கூந்தலின் நறியவும் உளவோ; Ainkurunuru 240 வண்டினம் மொய்ப்ப ... கூந்தல் நாறும்நின் மார்பே), and in 240 the scent is what reveals the union. The pairing is a shared image rather than one poem developing the other.

Both set இவ்வூர் against the lovers' word (Kural 1130 ஏதிலர் என்னும் இவ் வூர்; Ainkurunuru 110 இவ்வூர் பிறதொன் றாகக் கூறும்), and 110 appeals to பால் to make the bond real. But 110 does not say what the town says and its line 5 sense is uncertain, so the contrast is thinner than stated.
links.text_issue: Ainkurunuru 110 line 5 was repaired and the marker flagged its sense.

links.reason: Both measure suffering by one day against many (ஒருநாள் எழுநாள்போல்; உற்றது மன்னு மொருநாள் ... தவப்பன் னாள்), which is a real shared figure. But the poem does not limit the couplet; one is waiting time, the other the cost of a single union, so qualifies is the wrong type.

The parallel is real: Kuruntokai 69's மந்தி, கைம்மை உய்யா, leaps to death, and Perunkoppendu refuses the widow's rites for the pyre. But nothing in Kuruntokai 69 'borrows' from Purananuru 246; the teaches turns a parallel across domains into a borrowing.

Both marutham verses put the buffalo plunging into the pond in the man's town epithet (மதஎருமை தண்கயம் பாயும்; எருமை பழனம் படிந்து). But Ainthinai Ezhupathu 49 tells the bard only to tell the women about the ஊரன்; it does not state that the buffalo is his portrait, so it cannot prove the hidden sense of Kainnilai 37.

The same poet uses மலர்தலை உலகம் in both, and the idyll's kings who ruled உரைசெல and are more than திரையிடு மணல் are gone. But Purananuru 24 never says fame exempts from death; its famous ones are நின்று விளிந்தோர், who also died. The idyll does not show fame is 'common'; the teaches misstates the short poem.

Ainkurunuru 410's பொழுதிற்கு ஒத்தன்று is the old affirmative past (like நின்றன்று), 'was in keeping with the hour', so the bard's lute accompanied the family joy rather than being outdone by it. The note's 'the lute did not match' misreads the verb, and Kural 66's contrast with the child's prattle is not in the poem.

Kar Narpathu 4 calls the season பசலை மருந்து and Ainkurunuru 342 says அவரோ வாரார் தான்வந் தன்றே; the contrast of comfort and disappointment is real. But the poems are of different seasons and flowers (konrai in kar; nunavam in ilavenil), not 'the same flowering', and 342 does not call it a sickness.

The fragment says enemies have no course but பணிந்துவழி மொழிதல், set against the king's நிறைஅரும் சீற்றம்; Purananuru 17 gives the defeated kings' reasoning (பெறல் கூடும் இவன்நெஞ்சு உறப்பெறின்; உடன்று நோக்கினன்). The pair specifically shows submission as a calculation before the king's anger.
links.text_issue: Fragment 1 is a fragment and the marker flagged its sense.

links.reason: Kalittokai 11 has the stag give its shade (தன் நிழலைக் கொடுத்து அளிக்கும் கலை) and the tusker let the mate drink the little water first; Aimpathu 38's stag feigns drinking (கள்ளத்தின் ஊச்சும்) so the doe drinks the சிறுநீர். The same paalai proof of the road's tenderness is refined by the pretence; true and specific.

The two adjacent verses agree that tending guests is the wife's part (விருந்தஞ்சும் ஈர்வளை; நல்விருந் தோம்பலின் நட்டாளாம்). But 64 lists hospitality as one of three equal debts, and 63 lists the guest-fearing wife as one of three useless things, so 'first duty' and 'failing it alone' are not in the Tamil.

Kuruntokai 66 calls the konrai மடவ for taking the வம்ப மாரி for கார்; Kuruntokai 382 calls the rain வம்பு and argues from his absence (பருவம் ஆயின் வாராரோ). Both deny the season, but 382 makes his word the test of the rain, a real refinement.

Paripadal 9 has like outdo like (ஆடல் நவின்றோர் அவர் போர் செறுப்பவும் ... வல்லாரை வல்லார் செறுப்பவும்), and Paripadal 17 pairs each human sound with a thing of the hill (ஒருதிறம் ... ஒருதிறம்) in மாறு எதிர் கோடல். The teaches is true, but 17 extends 9's contest rather than limiting it.

Both poems reject the velan's divine cause, which is the stock veri situation. Ainkurunuru 250 describes Vel by his own peacock and valli (மடமயில் ஆலும் ... வள்ளியம் கானம் கிழவோன்) and denies him; only Akam 388 gives the god the lover's hunt, so 'each other's emblems' is untrue for 250.

The tiger-on-elephant image is shared (Kural 599 யானை வெரூஉம் புலிதாக் குறின்; Kalavazhi 16 horses on the குஞ்சரக் கும்பம் like வேங்கை இரும்புலி). But Kural 599 does not contain ஊக்கம; the word is the chapter title, so 'names the driving force with the Kural's own word' overstates.

The diction is shared and specific: வேறுபுலத்(து) இறுத்த ... தானை and வேறுபுலத்து இறுக்கும் தானை, மைந்துமலி and மைந்து மலிந்த, the bard's வந்தனென் ... கண்டனென் and வந்து இனிது காண்டிசின். The contrast கந்து சேர்பு நிலைஇ against கந்துகால் கீழ்ந்து is real in the Tamil.

நால்வேறு இயற்கைப் பதினொரு மூவர் is 33 in four kinds, and Paripadal 8 counts பதின்மரும் இருவரும் (12), மருந்து உரை இருவரும் (2), எண்மரும் (8), and the பன்னொருவர் of Aathirai's lord (11). Both make the gods come to Murugan; the pairing is accurate and specific.

Both have the vengai's fallen flowers look like a tiger (வேங்கை ஒள்வீப் புலிப்பொறி கடுப்ப; இளவேங்கை கான்றபூ ... வயவேங்கை ஏய்க்கும்), a distinctive image. In Akam 228 a she-elephant bolts; in Thinaimalai 26 the friend makes the false tiger the reason the girl will not live (வாழாள்) if he comes at night.

Purananuru 159 refuses a grudging gift (தவிர்ந்துவிடு பரிசில் கொள்ளலென்) but takes a kunri gladly given (உவந்து நீ இன்புற விடுதி யாயின்); Kural 1061 refuses even the glad giver (கரவாது உவந்தீயும் ... இரவாமை). A true tension on exactly the same case.

நகல் in Kural 860 is friendly gladness set against இகல், while நகுதல் in 784 is laughing together; the shared root has two senses, and the verses make no conflicting claim. The teaches only restates a shared word.

Kuruntokai 200 turns forgetting into a charge (மறந்தோர் மன்ற மறவா நாமே), proved by the rains that came (கால மாரி); Kural 1207 keeps it as her own impossibility (மறப்பின் எவனாவன் ... மறப்பறியேன்). The contrast of accusation and self-torment is specific and true.

Both Nallanthuvanar poems use மெல்லியான் பருவம்: in 129 darkness comes like the weak reign after a just king, in 120 the evening goes as the enemy over a weak reign is driven off when a நல் இறை appears with the lover's return. The political figure at both ends of the night is in the Tamil.

Akam 78 recalls Paari with வாய்மொழிக் கபிலன் சூழ, holding out யாண்டுபல and driving off the kings (வேந்தர் ஓட்டிய), and uses Paari's pool (பைஞ்சுனைப் பூத்த ... புதுமலர்) for the girl's brow; Purananuru 109 is Kapilar's boast in the siege, praising Paari's சுனை. The akam use of the puram fact is stated correctly.

Kuruntokai 140 asks how the town knew the grief she bore silently (யாங்கறிந் தன்றிவ் வழுங்க லூரே); Kural 1180 says secrets are not hard for the town to learn from அறைபறை கண்ணார். The couplet supplies an answer to the poem's question, a real and specific pairing.

Ainkurunuru 219 does join the leaving to the pallor (நாடன் பிரிந்தென ஒண்ணுதல் பசப்பது), and Kural 1188 complains that no one says துறந்தார் அவர். But the speaker of 219 is not fixed by அன்னாய், and one poem cannot show the friend as 'the one voice' that names the cause.

Naladiyar 370 makes புதுப்புனல் end with the rain; Paripadal 7 prays that the bathing not cease (நின் படிந்து நீங்காமை). A wish to keep bathing in the yearly flood does not deny that the flood ends, and line 85 is lacunose, so the 'reversal' is built on a shared word.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 7 line 85 has a gap; line 81 repaired.

links.reason: Kural 1189 accepts pallor if he is well (பசக்கமன் ... நன்னிலையர் ஆவர் எனின்); Kuruntokai 27 calls the beauty எனக்கு மாகாது என்னைக்கு முதவாது, milk spilt on the ground, eaten by பசலை. Sacrifice against sheer waste is a defensible tension about the same pallor.

The same poet uses the same formula for the man (கிளி கடிந்து ... நம்மொடு; கிள்ளை நம்மொடு கடிந்தோன்): in Natrinai 25 he leaves with no chance to speak, in Akam 242 the mother, not knowing he came in love (பண்புதர வந்தமை அறியாள்), calls the அறியா வேலன். The formula marks the friend's knowledge against the mother's ignorance.

Both compare the man to the sun (ஞாயி றனையன்; வெஞ்சுடர் அன்னான்). But Kuruntokai 315 says only நெருஞ்சி யனைய ... தோளே; that the nerunji 'turns after him' is a reading the Tamil does not fix, and Thinaimalai 89's sun and moon are a travellers' description of a couple, so 'dependence versus parity' needs a generous reading.
links.text_issue: Thinaimalai 89 line 2 is read only tentatively.

poems.note: The reed that serves bathing women as companion maps to the man and the women he keeps; with two parts mapped it is ullurai rather than iraicchi.
The crow stirring the backwater at midnight may hint at the prying town, but no one-sentence implication is fixed.
The field-of-the-ear figure is introduced by an explicit போல் in line 2.

iraicchi.act: the old lame heron carries sea fish to its pregnant mate who could not go to the grove
iraicchi.sense: even a crippled old heron provides for its mate, so the man should take her and care for her by marrying

poems.note: குயில் appears to be the subject of பொய்த்த, so striking it removes the stated charge of falsehood.
The heron is a literal witness of his oath; without it the question has no subject.
The elephant's victory is joined to explicit similes (குறங்கு அறுத்திடுவான் போல், மால் போல்) and maps to no second part of the love situation.

iraicchi.act: the paired anril feed in the backwater and roost together on the palmyra
iraicchi.sense: the pair that never parts shows the union the shore lord has taken from her

poems.note: The carrier is also the addressee; striking lines 1-2 removes the vocative but the message to the துறைவன் stands.

iraicchi.act: the heron sleeps in the sweet shade of the punnai
iraicchi.sense: the heron of his own shore sleeps while she, left by him, cannot

iraicchi.act: the hunter, his kill made, returns openly with his dog to his own hut and family
iraicchi.sense: the man should likewise come openly and take her to his home instead of coming by night

poems.note: The carrier is a person of the land rather than a creature; read as karupporul it passes.
The tiger hunting for its whelped mate is mainly the danger of his night path; its care for the mate gives no single implication.
The clouds are tied to Andiran's elephants by an explicit போல.
The sand doll with flower-freckled breasts maps to the girl now come of age and her watched body, pointing to the confinement named in the thurai.
Line 1 is obscure: what plunges into the pond is not named.
Puram by its colophon (வாகை, கூதிர்ப்பாசறை), so both are null.

vehicle: பெருங்களிறு வாங்க முரிந்துநிலம் படாஅ நாருடை ஒசியல்

poems.note: The wingless old heron fed by the fishers may hint at fading youth, but no single implication is fixed.
